You are helping with an AUTHORIZED, READ-ONLY security audit of a Next.js App Router codebase at /opt/nxeon. These files are `"use server"` action modules — every exported async function is a remotely-invokable HTTP endpoint an attacker can POST to directly with arbitrary arguments. DO NOT EDIT ANYTHING. Only Read/grep.

Auth model (from /opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts): `requireUser()` returns current user or throws; `requireAdmin()` throws unless role===ADMIN; `requireStaff()` staff-only. Admin/infrastructure capabilities MUST use requireAdmin (or requireStaff for support tooling), NOT requireUser. An action is IDOR-vulnerable if it acts on a caller-supplied id without an ownership/scope check. A dangerous action with only `requireUser` (or no guard) that controls infra, runs commands, writes files, or reads other users' data is a finding.

For EACH of these files:
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-abuse.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-backups-admin.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-nodes.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-files.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-coldemail.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-terminal.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-claude-console.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-sandbox.ts

Enumerate every EXPORTED async function that reaches a dangerous sink: `db.job.create` (root worker), `spawn`/`exec`/`execSync`, `writeFile`/SFTP write, command execution over SSH, minting tokens/credentials, or reading/writing files on a server. For each report EXACTLY:
- file:line and function name
- the auth guard present (quote the line), or NONE
- for functions taking an id/serverId: whether it verifies ownership (quote the line, or "NO OWNERSHIP CHECK")
- the sink reached (and if it runs a shell command, whether any user input is interpolated into the command string — quote it)
- VERDICT: OK / IDOR / NO-AUTH / WEAK (requireUser on an admin-only/infra capability) / CMD-INJECTION (unsanitized input into a shell string)

Quote real lines with numbers. actions-files.ts and actions-coldemail.ts: pay close attention to path/command construction and whether the target server/host is ownership-checked. actions-terminal.ts and actions-claude-console.ts: these may mint terminal tokens or run commands — check the guard and whether serverId ownership is verified. Tight bulleted list per file, most dangerous first. No speculation beyond the code.

7	 * subdomain namespaces (`FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain`
8	 * live in different tables but resolve under the same `play.nxeon.cloud` zone,
9	 * so a name taken in either one is unavailable in both). `excludeServerId`/
10	 * `excludeFreeMcId` let a rename check availability without tripping over the
11	 * row's own current value.
12	 *
13	 * Server-only (imports `./db`) — a client component must import
14	 * ./game-subdomain-rules directly for the format check instead.
15	 */
16	export async function isSubdomainAvailable(
17	  sub: string,
18	  opts?: { excludeServerId?: string; excludeFreeMcId?: string },
19	): Promise<boolean> {
20	  const [freeHit, paidHit] = await Promise.all([
21	    db.freeMinecraftServer.findFirst({
22	      where: { subdomain: sub, ...(opts?.excludeFreeMcId ? { id: { not: opts.excludeFreeMcId } } : {}) },
23	      select: { id: true },
24	    }),
25	    db.server.findFirst({
26	      where: { subdomain: sub, ...(opts?.excludeServerId ? { id: { not: opts.excludeServerId } } : {}) },
27	      select: { id: true },
28	    }),
29	  ]);
30	  return !freeHit && !paidHit;
31	}

17	/**
18	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
19	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
20	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
21	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
22	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
23	 */
24	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
25	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
26	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
27	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
28	}

40	/**
41	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
42	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
43	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
44	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
45	 */
46	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
47	  const inspect = await exec(
48	    conn,
49	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
50	    10_000,
51	  );
52	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
53	    return { running: false, players: null };
54	  }
55	  const status = await dockerExec(
56	    conn,
57	    containerName,
58	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
59	    10_000,
60	  );
61	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
62	  try {
63	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);
64	    const p = parsed?.server_info?.players;
65	    if (typeof p?.online === "number" && typeof p?.max === "number") {
66	      return { running: true, players: { online: p.online, max: p.max } };
67	    }
68	  } catch {
69	    /* fall through */
70	  }
71	  return { running: true, players: null };
72	}

74	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };

76	// Some plugins (EssentialsX's /list override is the one that's bitten us)
77	// colorize their command output with raw ANSI escape codes, which the RCON
78	// protocol passes straight through as literal bytes in the response text —
79	// there's no terminal on the other end to interpret them. Confirmed live: a
80	// player name came back as "papiguapo\x1b[0m", which then failed every
81	// caller's name validation (it's not alphanumeric) and broke the inventory
82	// editor's "pick a valid player" check even with a real player selected.
83	// Stripped once here so every RCON consumer (players list, Console tab,
84	// Roles, inventory editor) gets clean text for free.
85	const ANSI_ESCAPE_RE = /\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g;

87	/** One RCON round-trip via the bundled rcon-cli — see lib/game-control.ts's
88	 *  validateRconCommand for the same input sanitation used on the paid path. */
89	export async function sendRcon(
90	  conn: Client,
91	  containerName: string,
92	  ownerId: string,
93	  command: string,
94	): Promise<RconResult> {
95	  const password = rconPasswordFor(ownerId);
96	  const r = await dockerExec(
97	    conn,
98	    containerName,
99	    `env RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(password)} rcon-cli ${shellQuote(command)}`,
100	    12_000,
101	  );
102	  if (r.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: r.stderr.trim() || "RCON command failed." };
103	  return { ok: true, response: r.stdout.replace(ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, "").trim() };
104	}

108	/** Parses rcon-cli's `list` response: "There are N of a max of M players online: a, b, c" */
109	export async function getFreeServerPlayers(
110	  conn: Client,
111	  containerName: string,
112	  ownerId: string,
113	): Promise<{ ok: true; players: PlayerInfo[] } | { ok: false; error: string }> {
114	  const r = await sendRcon(conn, containerName, ownerId, "list");
115	  if (!r.ok) return r;
116	  const colonIdx = r.response.indexOf(":");
117	  if (colonIdx === -1) return { ok: true, players: [] };
118	  const names = r.response
119	    .slice(colonIdx + 1)
120	    .split(",")
121	    .map((s) => s.trim())
122	    .filter(Boolean);
123	  return { ok: true, players: names.map((name) => ({ name })) };
124	}

126	/** Reads /data/server.properties into a plain key->value map. */
127	export async function readServerProperties(
128	  conn: Client,
129	  containerName: string,
130	): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
131	  const r = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, "cat /data/server.properties", 10_000);
132	  if (r.code !== 0) return {};
133	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
134	  for (const line of r.stdout.split("\n")) {
135	    if (!line || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
136	    const i = line.indexOf("=");
137	    if (i === -1) continue;
138	    out[line.slice(0, i).trim()] = line.slice(i + 1).trim();
139	  }
140	  return out;
141	}

143	/**
144	 * Writes a set of server.properties keys in place (sed-style line replace,
145	 * appending any key not already present) and restarts the container so the
146	 * itzg entrypoint's normal boot sequence picks the new values up — the image
147	 * only reads server.properties at startup (confirmed against the Minecraft
148	 * wiki: none of gamemode/motd/max-players/etc. persist a live RCON change back
149	 * to the file), so a restart is the only fully-reliable way to apply anything
150	 * here. Keys with a real live RCON equivalent (difficulty, whitelist on/off)
151	 * are ALSO pushed live by the caller for instant effect — see FIELD_LIVE_CMD.
152	 */
153	export async function writeServerProperties(
154	  conn: Client,
155	  containerName: string,
156	  changes: Record<string, string>,
157	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
158	  const current = await readServerProperties(conn, containerName);
159	  const merged = { ...current, ...changes };
160	  const body = Object.entries(merged)
161	    .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`)
162	    .join("\n");
163	  const write = await execInput(
164	    conn,
165	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c 'cat > /data/server.properties'`,
166	    body + "\n",
167	    10_000,
168	  );
169	  if (write.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: write.stderr.trim() || "Could not write server.properties." };
170	  return { ok: true };
171	}

202	/** Translates a preset's `properties` map into the itzg env vars a fresh
203	 *  `docker run` needs to boot with those settings already applied. */
204	export function propertiesToEnv(properties: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string> {
205	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
206	  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(properties)) {

209	  }

738	 * itself is full of `&` colour codes, which `sed`'s replacement syntax treats
739	 * as "insert the matched text" unless individually escaped — a real footgun
740	 * for a value built from data, not a fixed literal. Read+regex+writeback (via
741	 * execInput's stdin path, same mechanism as writeServerProperties) sidesteps
742	 * that whole class of shell/sed escaping bug entirely. Live-verified this
743	 * session: a config patched this way survives an immediate `docker restart`
744	 * (the same restart applyModeProperties always does right after this runs)
745	 * with no YAML parse errors and Essentials fully re-enabling.

747	async function patchEssentialsJoinMessage(
748	  conn: Client,
749	  containerName: string,
750	  message: string,
751	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
752	  const path = "/data/plugins/Essentials/config.yml";
753	  const read = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, `cat ${path}`, 10_000);
754	  if (read.code !== 0) {
755	    return { ok: false, error: read.stderr.trim() || "Could not read Essentials config.yml" };
756	  }
757	  // YAML double-quoted scalar: only \ and " need escaping (our messages never
758	  // contain either today, but a future edit might).
759	  const yamlValue = message.replace(/\\/g, "\\\\").replace(/"/g, '\\"');
760	  const patched = read.stdout.replace(/^custom-join-message:.*$/m, `custom-join-message: "${yamlValue}"`);
761	  if (patched === read.stdout) {
762	    return { ok: false, error: "custom-join-message key not found in Essentials config.yml" };
763	  }
764	  const write = await execInput(
765	    conn,
766	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c ${shellQuote(`cat > ${path}`)}`,
767	    patched,
768	    10_000,
769	  );
770	  if (write.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: write.stderr.trim() || "Could not write Essentials config.yml" };

776	/**
777	 * Polls until the Minecraft server inside `containerName` has actually
778	 * finished booting (its log prints "Done (Ns)!") or gives up.
779	 *
780	 * This exists because BOTH of the "is it ready" checks it replaces were too
781	 * shallow: `docker inspect ...State.Running` only proves the container
782	 * PROCESS hasn't crashed — a plugin-heavy boot spends 40-90s downloading and
783	 * loading before the game itself is reachable, and that whole window used to
784	 * read as "ready". Worse, mc-router's own wake check has the identical gap:
785	 * it just opens a raw TCP connection to :25565, and Minecraft's listener
786	 * binds early, well before world/plugin loading finishes — so the port looks
787	 * "up" long before the server can actually complete a client handshake. Both
788	 * gaps together are exactly what produced a real, reproduced-live customer
789	 * bug: switching to SkyBlock reported success, mc-router's TCP check passed
790	 * within seconds, and the customer's client still got "Failed to connect —
791	 * Timed out" because the server was still mid-boot. Polling the log line
792	 * itself is the only signal that means what it says.
793	 *
794	 * `docker restart` re-runs the exact same boot sequence as a fresh `docker
795	 * run`, so this same wait is needed after `applyModeProperties`'s restart
796	 * too, not just the initial container creation.
797	 */
798	async function waitForServerReady(
799	  conn: Client,
800	  containerName: string,
801	  // 110s covers a plain/properties-only boot with room to spare. A "plugins"
802	  // preset installs its Modrinth projects (download + Paper plugin-loader
803	  // init) BEFORE the JVM's own "Done (Xs)!" timer even starts counting, which
804	  // a live, reproduced customer failure showed can push total wall-clock time
805	  // past 110s even when the JVM's own boot only reports ~76s — this function
806	  // was giving up ~2s before a real, healthy SkyBlock server finished
807	  // starting, deleting its DB row while the container kept running, orphaned
808	  // (invisible to the customer, indefinitely occupying a capacity slot).
809	  // Callers pass FREEMC_PLUGIN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS for any "plugins"-kind preset.
810	  timeoutMs = 110_000,
811	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
812	  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
813	  // First few seconds are the container just starting up (image entrypoint,
814	  // ownership fix, etc.) — no point polling logs before that's underway.
815	  await sleep(3_000);
816	  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
817	    const running = await exec(conn, `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`, 10_000);
818	    if (running.code !== 0 || running.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
819	      return { ok: false, error: "Container exited before finishing startup." };
820	    }
821	    const logs = await exec(conn, `docker logs ${shellQuote(containerName)} --tail 200 2>&1`, 10_000);
822	    if (/\bDone \([\d.]+s\)!/.test(logs.stdout)) return { ok: true };
823	    await sleep(3_000);
824	  }
825	  return { ok: false, error: "Server took too long to start." };
826	}
